description.purpose: Context assembly as a hive: it gathers what an LLM needs of one round -- the turn that opened it, the memory leg, the brief, the tool round fanned back in -- and passes all of it on uncut (R-27-1, GH #889). Everything of a round leaves through ONE message on route `curate` to the `curator` template, which decides what enters the model's context window; the same seam ends a runaway tool round at `max_iter` on `answer`, so a later split of the agent behind that seam does not re-cut the collector. A round that loses a tool result exits deterministically past an idle window (synthetic error results, round_stale=1), and a user turn arriving mid-round defers instead of opening a second assembly - decided behaviour where there used to be accident. The rows of a round fall when it ends; only the session's `depart` rows outlive it, holding the three newest consult ids an advisor has answered under and the mark that the other side of a peer channel spoke, each falling after seven days on its own clock; a round nothing else ends falls at the next turn-open once its last row is older than `max(10 × round_idle_ms, 10 × late_after_ms, 10 min)`. Moved to `curator` in `collector@5.0.0` (GH #889): the rolling conversation window, the close batch `write` and the per-turn episodes `turn_write`. Removed in `collector@5.0.0` (GH #889): the caps over every leg, the curation of 1.1.0 and 3.1.0 (GH #451) -- the budget projection, its stages and recovery stubs, `recoverability`, `keep_rounds`, the `system.budget` sentence -- and the prune lane with its `batched` ledger. Moved to `curator` in `collector@5.0.0` (GH #889): the `in_pack` lane of 3.2.0 ([#458](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/458), [#488](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/488)) with its closed list (`identity`, `persona`, `handover`, `instructions`) and its `pack_ack` receipt. Since 3.3.0 ([#464](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/464)) the tool menu is ASKED FOR instead of typed: `params.tools` is the list of names the agent's own template says it uses, a tick on `in_menu_tick` sends exactly those names to the tools hive, and the answer comes back on `in_menu` and leaves on `menu` as durable `system.tools`, which the curator keeps for the brain since `collector@5.0.0` (GH #889) -- one write, not a per-turn cost. Removed in `collector@5.0.0` (GH #889): `tool_menu`, the manual override that switched the asking off. A declared name the hive has nothing under comes back in `hop.menu_unknown` and as a warn line, never as a silence. Two accepted lanes and two emitted ones is the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a) -- nothing that shipped changed behaviour, and a collector that declares no tools behaves exactly as 3.2.0 did. The menu kept the tools this hive answered itself (3.3.1, [#512](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/512)): `memory_recall` left with `collector@4.0.0` (GH #552) and `thread_recall` with `collector@5.0.0` (GH #889), so no self-served name is left. Since 3.4.0 ([#529](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/529)) that menu is a UNION over ANSWERERS instead of one answer. Before it, one reply WAS the menu -- parse, add the self-served names, write the lot with `$replace` -- which is right while exactly one thing answers and is the whole defect the moment two do: the second reply would not merge with the first, it would delete it, and the two would take the menu away from each other on every tick forever. A second answerer is now required, because a tool the composite reaches by an edge on its NAME is topology of the level that draws the edge and only the side that ANSWERS it can declare it. So each answerer's last submenu is kept as one row of this hive's own store, keyed by `context.tool_answerer` -- the mirror of the `tool_caller` the request already carries -- and every answer re-derives the menu from all the rows, ordered by answerer so the same rows always produce the same menu. An answer with no answerer on it is the one-answerer shape and counts as the default one, so a tree wired before this behaves exactly as it did. Two consequences fall out: `menu_unknown` is computed against the MERGED menu, so a name one answerer has nothing under but another delivers is not a finding; and a store that refuses the merge is a warn line and a stop rather than a `degraded` answer, because a menu is durable state with no turn beside it and the next tick asks again. A second store table and a new phase is the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a) -- nothing a caller sends or receives changed shape. Since 3.5.0 a round that spends its ITERATION budget ends on a named PARTIAL ANSWER instead of on the raw end of the tool round (GH #570): the seam appends one assistant text turn saying which bound it hit, how many calls it made, which tools it called and the head of the last result, and stamps `hop.partial`. What a consumer reads is the LAST text of an answer, so a capped round used to hand a surface a raw tool payload and the person was shown a search dump -- the better the errand was going, the more certainly a tool got quoted at the reader. The raw round is untouched and leaves on the same `answer`. `hop.partial` is the marker `round_capped` could never be: until `collector@5.0.0` that key also meant that some bytes were trimmed off a round still going (GH #889 removed the caps), and only an early end is an answer somebody is looking at. A new hop key and a text promise nothing made before is the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a). Since 4.0.0 the ask has a CAUSE instead of a cadence (GH #553): the hive accepts `mutation_committed` -- the mutation door's receipt, carried in by the level above -- and its own door turns it into the internal `in_menu_tick` the `./menu-clock` timer used to stamp. The timer is gone; the boot receipt is the first ask, so an agent has its menu before its first turn, and a tool added by mutation reaches it with the receipt of that very mutation. Since 1.2.0 every knob of this cell is a PARAM read off the stdin document rather than a `COLLECTOR_*` substitution token out of the colony's environment ([#138](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/138)), and this template is the REFERENCE migration for the move: two collectors in one colony are tuned apart without a fork of the script, and there is no environment fallback left to read. Since 4.1.0 the collector no longer TYPES the block contract it asks a brain for ([#606](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/606)). Until 4.0.0 it held the memory hive's annotation rules as a literal and wrote them to `system.instructions.sidecar` on every turn assembly, which put the rules of a memory in a cell that enforces none of them and could describe exactly one consumer. The sections are OFFERED now: the `tool_schemas` answer carries `sidecar[]` -- `{section, required, schema, instruction}` -- beside `schemas[]`, merged over the answerers by section name exactly as the tool menu is merged by tool name (GH #529), and this cell composes ONE contract out of them: a preamble it COMPOSES (the frame every section shares, then the whole-object shape of this composition and the obligation with the section names in it -- 494 characters for the shipped pair, and its last two lines are repairs the harness bought: a model that dropped the outer braces and a model that let the optional section stand instead of the required one), then `## <section> (required|optional)` with the offering template's own words and a compact example rendered from its schema, required first and alphabetical inside each half, under the ceiling `params.sidecar_max_chars` (optional sections fall from the back with a warn line; a required one never falls). The result rides on the `menu` message beside `system.tools`: the same durability class, one write per change and nothing per turn, re-derived on every mutation receipt -- which keeps the GH #525 property that a brain whose birth is behind it still receives it. The knob `inline_extraction` is called `sidecar` and nobody offering anything writes an EMPTY slot rather than falling silent, because durable state is revoked and never merely abandoned. A renamed knob and a widened lane are the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a). Since 4.2.0 it also assembles for a brain that is not ANSWERING anybody. In a duplex voice session the model on the wire speaks to the caller itself and the brain behind this cell advises it, so three things join: `system.instructions.mode` says which job the round is -- the advise charter when `context.engine` is `duplex`, an empty text otherwise, written on every assembly because a slot that is only ever set would keep advising a brain for the rest of its life; the lane `in_delegation` takes the errand the model hands the backend of its own accord, assembled exactly like `in_advice` under role `delegation` and, like it, never drained into a memory, because the errand is the model's own and a memory that kept it would hand it back to the caller as her own word; and an `in_turn` carrying `messages[user, assistant]` is written as the PAIR it is, two rows under one `turn_id` in the same bundle, with the answer row's id derived from the question's so the two cannot travel in the order two random ids compare in. A duplex turn is cut on the MODEL's clock and arrives whole; a turn with only a question is written exactly as it always was. A new accepted lane, a new unconditional slot and a widened `in_turn` are the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a) -- nothing that shipped changed behaviour. Still inside 4.2.0 ([#799](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/799)) the SHAPE LINE of the preamble prints the form each offer actually takes -- `{...}` for an object, `"..."` for a sentence -- where it printed `{...}` for every section whatever the schema said. The advise sections of `talky` are strings, so the frame asked a model to nest one, and the splitter one hop down dropped what did not fit. No lane, no knob and no address moves, and 4.2.0 has not shipped, so the number is extended rather than superseded -- which is also what keeps `templates/cogny/collector` out of it. 4.3.0 adds the THIRD leg of a turn ([#834](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/834)): with the knob `brief_slots` set and a `context.counterpart` -- an entity reference the entry edge of a channel with many counterparts stamps -- the turn's opening raises `brief` beside `recall`, the fan-in waits for `leg-brief`, the answer comes home on `in_briefing` and reaches the brain as a synthetic `affinity_brief` tool pair, never as `system.*`; an error is an empty leg, and a turn without a counterpart parks the leg empty and waits for nothing. A caller can do something it never could, so it is the second digit; `assemble`'s contract moves to 2.2.0. 4.4.0 says how an answer ended ([#843](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/843)): every `answer` carries `hop.finish_reason` -- `stop`, `length`, or empty where the cell knows no reason (a spent round's digest, a store report) -- and `hop.truncated`, `"1"` when the completion was cut on `length`, so a consumer can refuse or mark a half sentence instead of passing it on as complete. And the three round lanes that park a message without a turn id (`in_calls`, `in_tool`, `in_answer`) now say so on stderr ([#841](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/841)) -- until then that was the one silent refusal of the cell, and a `memory_recall` result stamped with an empty turn id vanished there. A caller can read something it never could, so it is the second digit; `assemble`'s contract moves to 2.3.0. In the same 4.4.0 a channel narrows the tool menu of its sessions ([#845](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/845)): `context.tools_allow`/`context.tools_deny`, stamped by the channel edge and read on `in_turn` only, are kept in a `session` row and sent with every brain call of the session as the body key `tool_scope` -- the `llm` cell filters that one request and the durable menu stays whole, so two turns of a session reach the provider with the same prefix; a changed scope is taken over and said (stderr, `hop.scope_changed`). And the other side of a peer or group channel has a role of its own ([#847](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/847)): every `origin: "peer"` turn is a `peer` row with `speaker`/`speaker_ref` -- from affinity's `who` or from a trusted gate, never from the text -- never the agent's own answer, framed on the wire by the `llm` cell; `system.roster` is the legend `<ref> = <name> (<identity>)` of the session and changes only on a join or a leave, `system.instructions.peer` states the fixed rule, and the memory drains a peer turn in full with its source. Moved to `curator` in `collector@5.0.0` (GH #889): an earlier answer keeping its block (4.4.1, [#871](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/871)) -- the collector keeps no earlier answer, so the window that shows one with its block is the curator's.
description.use_when: One per agent brain, between the inbound surface and the curator in front of the LLM. It replaces the pattern where a persona cell injects the system prompt, a prep cell mints the turn id and a third cell fans tool results in: those are one concern and this is it. Wire the entry lanes and the exit routes in the SAME mutation that instantiates it - an island without a crossing edge stays inactive.
description.not_in_scope: No inference and no persona (identity is not context assembly). No tool fan-OUT: routing a tool_call to the right tool stays a dispatcher's job, the collector only fans the results back in and answers no tool call itself (`memory_recall` is the memory hive's since GH #552; `thread_recall` was removed in `collector@5.0.0`, GH #889). No session lifecycle: a keeper decides when a generation begins and ends, and the close request is the `curator` template's since `collector@5.0.0` (GH #889). No memory judgement: the collector READS the recall bundle and nothing else. No window, no cap and no LLM judgement anywhere: every item of a round leaves whole on `curate`, and what enters the model's window is the curator's (R-27-1, GH #889). No second body format for a tool result: a result is the `tool_result` turns of its `messages[]` and nothing else. A `system` slot on the in_tool lane is dropped, and that is not an oversight (GH #252): `system.*` leaving the seam is state the curator keeps per family for the brain and outlives the round that wrote it, so nothing that is the evidence of ONE round belongs there. Since 2.1.0 that rule has no exception left - the memory bundle was the one carve-out and does not live in system.* either any more, it arrives as a synthetic memory_recall tool result inside the round it was fetched for, and what stays under system.memory is the revocation of that slot (GH #278). Moved to `curator` in `collector@5.0.0` (GH #889): the `in_pack` lane and the question who may open it (GH #458).
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the HIVE path (`params.ports` is empty since GH #228; an edge naming ./assemble or ./window is refused with hive_port_boundary), and what a caller wants rides on hop.route. Entry (the parent edge names the lane via set_hop route and promotes session_id): in_turn (an inbound user turn), in_advice (an advisor core's answer, arriving after its turn ended), in_delegation (an errand the duplex voice model hands the backend of its own accord), in_bundle (the memory hive's recall bundle), in_briefing (affinity's brief of the turn's counterpart, GH #834), in_calls (the assistant tool_call turn from a dispatcher), in_tool (one tool result: every turn of its messages[], filed under the call id each turn answers -- a result that answers two calls in one message closes both, and a `system` slot or a top-level body slot on a result is dropped at the lane on purpose, GH #252), in_answer (the brain's final turn), in_round_sweep (a timer's or operator's stuck-round re-check, hop.route == 'sweep'), in_menu (the tools hive's declarations coming back, GH #464), mutation_committed (the mutation door's receipt, carried in by the level above -- the hive's own door turns it into the internal in_menu_tick, GH #553). Exit (from the hive path, on hop.route): 'curate' -> the curator's in_curate lane (the running round, whole, in place of 'brain' since GH #889; the caller's edge carries the iteration bound and restore_ttl), 'answer' -> the reply sink (a real answer, a capped round with hop.partial=1, or a store refusal with hop.degraded=1 -- a reply edge guards on both keys, GH #343), 'recall' -> the memory hive's recall port (the per-turn leg when params.memory_tier is set; promote recall_query / memory_tier / recall_window_from / recall_window_to / session_id / turn_id / iter), 'brief' -> the member's affinity (only with params.brief_slots set and a context.counterpart, GH #834), 'schemas' -> a tools hive's in_schemas door, 'menu' -> the curator's in_slots lane (durable system.tools and the block contract beside it). Moved to `curator` in `collector@5.0.0` (GH #889): in_close with 'write', and 'turn_write'. Removed in `collector@5.0.0` (GH #889): in_thread_call, and in_prune with 'prune'.

turn 3 of a session references turn 1: the collector sends turn 3's round on 'curate', whole, and turns 1..3 reach the context through the curator's window -- the collector reads no earlier turn back (GH #889)

2 parallel tool calls: 1 assistant row + 2 tool rows in the round table, the guarded update wins once, and the re-entry carries the turn, the memory leg AND the tool round through the same seam ('curate')
a tool that answers two calls in ONE message: both results are filed under their own tool_call_id, the round is complete and fires -- the lane keeps the whole messages[], not its first turn
a 100 KB tool result reaches 'curate' whole, inside its round -- what of it the model's window can afford is the curator's decision (GH #889)

a model that will not stop asking for tools: at params.max_iter the seam emits route 'answer' with what it collected instead of a further round on 'curate', its last turn a named partial answer (hop.partial=1)
a round's answer leaves on 'answer' and the rows of that round fall in the same step -- the history, the close batch 'write' and the episodes are the curator's (GH #889)

a tool dies mid-flight and one result never arrives: the round parks, and the next turn, the next result or an in_round_sweep request after params.round_idle_ms closes it - the missing call is answered synthetically under its own tool_call_id and the round fires with round_stale=1
a user turn lands while a round is running: it is written and stamped deferred (no second assembly on the session), and rides with the next regular assembly marked round_deferred=1

the model wants memory about a TIME RANGE: it emits a memory_recall tool_call, the dispatcher routes it by hop.tool_name like any other tool, and the memory hive answers it (GH #552) -- the result comes back as an ordinary tool result under the original tool_call_id, so the round ends where it began (GH #78)
